# 03-upgrade-web-project: Upgrade ContosoUniversity to net10.0

Retarget `ContosoUniversity.csproj` to `net10.0` and resolve all resulting package and API issues in the same pass (Resolve Inline / Fix Inline — no stubs, no deferred work).

**Package work** (37 issues): several packages (`Microsoft.AspNet.Mvc`, `Microsoft.AspNet.Razor`, `Microsoft.AspNet.WebPages`, `Microsoft.AspNet.Web.Optimization`, `Microsoft.CodeDom.Providers.DotNetCompilerPlatform`, `Microsoft.Web.Infrastructure`, `NETStandard.Library`, and several `System.*` BCL packages) are framework-included on `net10.0` and should be removed rather than upgraded; `Antlr` needs replacing with `Antlr4`; the `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.*` family, `Microsoft.Extensions.*` family, `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`, `Microsoft.Bcl.*`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, and remaining `System.*` packages upgrade to their `net10.0`-compatible versions per [the project's package table](assessment/projects/ContosoUniversity.md#nuget-package-issues).

**API work** (569 issues, dominated by `System.Web.*`): the ASP.NET MVC 5 surface (`ViewResult`, `ActionResult`, `Controller.View`, `ModelState`, `ModelStateDictionary`, `ViewBag`, `SelectList`, `RedirectToAction`, etc. — 87% of all API issues) has no direct .NET 10 equivalent; introduce the **System.Web Adapters** package to bridge the remaining `System.Web`-dependent code onto ASP.NET Core hosting rather than a full architectural rewrite of the controller layer. `System.Messaging.MessageQueue` (MSMQ, 57 issues / 10%) has no .NET 10 API — replace usage with a supported message-queue client (e.g., an Azure Service Bus or RabbitMQ SDK) or isolate it behind an abstraction if a queue migration is out of scope for this pass; flag any MSMQ code where the concrete queue replacement needs a follow-up decision. Legacy `app.config`/`Web.config`-based configuration reads (16 issues) move to `System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager` (as an interim bridge) or `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration` where practical.

**Binding redirects**: 12 issues exist today (6 mandatory manual-redirect/auto-generation conflicts for `Newtonsoft.Json`, `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions`, `System.ComponentModel.Annotations`, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`, `System.Memory`, `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`; 6 potential downgrade issues on the same set). Per the confirmed option, document each existing redirect and its conflict/downgrade status before deciding whether to remove it — SDK-style + `net10.0` projects do not use `bindingRedirect`/`assemblyBinding` the same way as .NET Framework, so most existing entries are expected to become obsolete, but confirm none masks a real runtime dependency before deleting.

**Done when**: `ContosoUniversity.csproj` targets `net10.0`, all package references are resolved (upgraded, replaced, or removed as framework-included), all flagged API issues are fixed inline (including System.Web Adapters integration and MSMQ replacement/isolation), binding redirects are documented with a removal recommendation per entry, and the project builds with 0 errors.

## Research Findings (confirmed against repo, 2026-09-21)

- **Project state**: `ContosoUniversity.csproj` is already SDK-style (`Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web"`, `OutputType=Library`), targeting `net48`. 45 `PackageReference` entries confirmed (matches assessment total). No pre-existing `// STUB:` markers anywhere in the project (grep for `// STUB:` returned empty) — no stub-resolution decomposition applies.
- **Controllers (7)**: `BaseController.cs`, `CoursesController.cs`, `DepartmentsController.cs`, `HomeController.cs`, `InstructorsController.cs`, `NotificationsController.cs`, `StudentsController.cs` — all under `Controllers/`. Matching view folders exist under `Views/` (`Courses/`, `Departments/`, `Home/`, `Instructors/`, `Notifications/`, `Students/`, `Shared/`), plus `Views/Web.config` (Razor view config with its own `<appSettings>`) and `Views/_ViewStart.cshtml`.
- **MSMQ usage isolated to one file**: `Services/NotificationService.cs` — uses `MessageQueue`, `MessageQueue.Exists/Create`, `MessageQueueAccessRights`, `MessageQueueException`, `MessageQueueErrorCode`. `System.Messaging` reference is a plain `<Reference>` in the csproj (not a NuGet package). This is the only MSMQ consumer in the codebase.
- **Legacy config usage** (beyond `Web.config` itself): `Data/SchoolContextFactory.cs` and `Global.asax.cs` both call `ConfigurationManager.ConnectionStrings["DefaultConnection"]`; `Services/NotificationService.cs` calls `ConfigurationManager.AppSettings["NotificationQueuePath"]`. `Web.config` has `<appSettings>`; `Web.Debug.config`/`Web.Release.config` transforms exist (config-transform migration also needed).
- **Bundling**: `App_Start/BundleConfig.cs` uses `System.Web.Optimization` (`BundleCollection`, `ScriptBundle`, `StyleBundle`) — package `Microsoft.AspNet.Web.Optimization` is one of the framework-included/removal candidates; views likely reference `@Scripts.Render`/`@Styles.Render` (not yet grepped per-view — part of the web-migration subtask's own research).
- **Packages**: current csproj confirms all package names named in the task description (`Antlr`, `Microsoft.AspNet.Mvc/Razor/WebPages/Web.Optimization`, `Microsoft.Bcl.*`, `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient*`, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.*` (3.1.32), `Microsoft.Extensions.*` (3.1.32), `Microsoft.Web.Infrastructure`, `NETStandard.Library`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, several `System.*` BCL packages, `WebGrease`). Per assessment: 45 total packages, 24 need upgrade, 1 incompatible (`Antlr` → replace with `Antlr4`), rest either compatible or framework-included-on-net10 removals.
- **Binding redirects**: assessment reports 12 issues (6 mandatory, 6 potential) but no `<runtime><assemblyBinding>` section was found in a quick scan of `Web.config` — confirm/document during the package-work subtask directly against the assessment's binding-redirect detail.

## Decomposition Verdict: ESCALATED — broken down via TaskBreaker

Scenario `breakdown-hints/framework-web-migration.md` and `breakdown-hints/common.md` (loaded per Execution Stage Section 5) trigger:
- `web-controller-migration-units` — **MUST** (7 controllers, >5 threshold)
- `system-messaging-replacement` — **MUST** (MSMQ present, needs isolated technology-decision subtask)
- `web-config-to-appsettings` — **SHOULD** (config-transform files present: `Web.Debug.config`/`Web.Release.config`)
- `web-bundling-and-static-assets` — **SHOULD** (`System.Web.Optimization` bundling present)
- `large-package-replacement-batch` — **SHOULD** (37 package issues incl. one true replacement — Antlr → Antlr4 — requiring research)

Combined with the task's own stated size (37 package issues + 569 API issues + MSMQ + config migration + binding-redirect documentation across a single project with 7 controllers and full System.Web Adapters bridging), this is not one coherent unit of work. Escalated to `TaskBreaker` to split by concern: TFM+packages, System.Web Adapters/MVC surface (per-controller), MSMQ replacement, config/binding-redirect documentation.
